The /api/organizations/[id]/sharing-settings route is crudRoutes over the organizations table wrapped by requireOwnOrganizationItem: it never reads or writes organization_sharing_settings, answers GET with the organizations row of the own organization instead of the sharing flags, refuses PATCH and DELETE with 403 because the organizations table is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance table, and exports no PUT although the sharing settings form sends PUT, so the sharing flags (federation, sector, province and congress sharing, anonymization, approval) cannot be read or changed through the HTTP surface and no sharing decision is recorded.

The GET of the access-logs route (declared member floor, raised to steward by the low-role guard because the organizations table has email, phone and address columns) and of the sharing-settings route (admin floor) return the complete organizations row of the own organization (settings JSON, billing_contact_id, subscription tier, enabled features, created_by, legacy_org_id, contact fields) under the name of an access log and of sharing settings, so a steward who opens the access-log tab receives billing and configuration data that the name does not announce and that the admin-floor item route is meant to restrict.

The access-logs route configures PATCH at the steward write floor and the sharing-settings route at the admin floor over the organizations table with no blocked patch fields, and both configure the administrator DELETE that archives the organization; the only thing that makes them answer 403 today is the entry of organizations in the READ_ONLY list of the CRUD governance table, so one edit of that list would let a steward rewrite parent_id, status, settings and slug of the organization through a route named for logs, bypassing the system-administrator check that the organizations item route applies to parent and status.

Every GET over organizing_campaigns (the campaigns, card-check, support-percentage, workplace-mapping, committee, labour-board, nlrb-filings, forms/generate, notes, sequences, enrolment and assignments routes, collection and item) is configured at readRole member, and the table has no user, member, email or phone column, so the low-role guard opens it: any member of the organization, not only the organizing team or a steward, receives the campaign rows with target employer, workplace location, organizing strategy, key issues, employer vulnerabilities, union advantages, lead organizer and organizing team identifiers, estimated unit size, cards signed, signing progress, contacts identified and committed, filing, election and certification dates and vote counts, with no confidentiality column, no team-membership check and no read audit.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any member of an organization, whatever their role, calls GET on any of the fifteen organizing route files: readRole is member, the generic factory scopes the rows to the session organization and applies no owner or team condition because organizing_campaigns has no user, member, email or phone column, and it returns 50 rows per page by default (100 at most) with strategy text, employer vulnerabilities, organizing team identifiers, card counts and election figures.

potentialImpact.description: A member who is not on the organizing team, including one who reports to or sympathizes with the target employer, learns who leads and staffs a confidential campaign, how many cards are signed, which employer vulnerabilities the union plans to use and the planned filing and election dates; disclosure of organizing strategy and support to an employer exposes workers and organizers to retaliation and lets the employer mount a counter-campaign.

existingContainment.summary: The factory adds an organization predicate from the session organization, so the rows read are those of the caller own organization only; nothing narrows them to the organizing team, a steward or a classification, so the exposure is every campaign of the organization to every member.

releaseDisposition.justification: Campaign strategy, support counts and organizer identities are the data whose disclosure to an employer causes retaliation, and the routes serve them to every authenticated member of the organization at the lowest role floor with no team or classification condition; the tenant predicate keeps other organizations out but does not limit a same-organization reader, so the read blocks release until the institution names who may read a campaign.

defectRegister.title: The card-check, support-percentage, workplace-mapping, committee, labour-board, nlrb-filings, forms/generate, notes, sequences, sequences enrolment and assignments routes are all crudRoutes over the single organizing_campaigns table: none reads or writes a card, signer, committee member, workplace contact, note, sequence, enrolment, filing or form, none applies the campaignId, viewType, groupBy, noteType, sentiment or followUpPending parameters its clients send, and each answers 200 with campaign rows or creates a campaign row from the body, so a capability whose real state is not implemented is returned as a successful response under the name of card check, support percentage, mapping, committee, filings, notes, sequences and enrolment.

POST and PATCH on organizing_campaigns copy the body into the row, so a steward sets cards_signed, card_signing_progress, target_card_count, contacts_identified, contacts_committed, filing_date, election_eligible_voters, votes_for_union, votes_against_union, challenged_ballots, election_result, certification_date and status to any value: no card, signer or ballot record exists to derive or verify them, the progress percentage is not computed from cards_signed and the estimated unit size, a count above the unit size is accepted, and cards_signed and card_signing_progress are the only support figures any of these routes stores or returns, so a typed-in number is what a reader receives as the card count and support level of the campaign.

The labour-board and nlrb-filings routes record no filing: GET lists organizing_campaigns rows and POST inserts one from the body and answers success, no filing row, filing identifier, board, receipt or status is stored, nothing is transmitted to a labour board or the NLRB, and the filing wizard (which posts a filing shape with filingType, jurisdiction, unit description and card submission fields) carries none of the required campaign columns, so its post fails on the insert and its alert reports a failed submission, so a filing is neither drafted nor sent, while a campaign-shaped body is accepted as a success under the name of a filing.

The forms/generate route generates no form: GET lists organizing_campaigns rows and POST inserts a campaign row from the body or fails on its required columns (the form generator posts campaignId, templateId and formData, none of which is a campaign column), it returns JSON and never a PDF, no template or legal text exists on the server, and the form generator reads the response with blob() without checking the status and saves it as a PDF named for the form type and employer, so an error or JSON body is downloaded as a labour board form.

The item routes under notes/[id], sequences/[id], sequences/[id]/enroll and assignments/[id] take a campaign id as the path id: PATCH at the steward floor rewrites any column of the whole campaign (status, lead organizer, organizing team, outcome figures, archived_at), and DELETE at the admin floor sets the campaign status to archived, so a call to delete a note, a sequence or an enrolment archives the campaign with no reason or confirmation, archived_at is not set, and the archived campaign is still returned by every GET because the read filters no status.

campaign_code on organizing_campaigns is unique across all organizations and is a required column the body must supply, as are campaign_name, target_employer, workplace_location and estimated_unit_size: a code already used by another organization, a repeated code or a body missing a required column makes the insert fail and the route answers an unexplained 500 instead of a conflict or a validation error, and an otherwise complete body that fails because its code is already used by another organization reveals that the code exists outside the caller organization.

The assignments routes assign nobody: an assignment is the lead_organizer_id column (a foreign key to profiles) and the organizing_team uuid array on the campaign row, which POST and PATCH at the steward floor set to any value from the body, with no check that the user is a member or an organizer of the organization, that the organizing_team ids exist, or that the person accepted, and with no assignment history, so any steward can name or remove the lead and team of any campaign in the organization.

The labour board form generator calls /api/organizing/campaigns/<campaignId>, an item path that the repository has no route for (the campaigns route file has no item route), and the organizing console and campaign detail console call /api/v2/organizing/campaigns, which the v2 catch-all answers with a 200 deprecation notice and no campaign data, so those clients load no campaign through the route that exists and show an empty or unpopulated state.

The organizer/impact route is crudRoutes over organizer_tasks: GET returns organizer task rows and POST inserts a task from the body, it reads no case, grievance or satisfaction data, applies no period parameter and returns no current or previous impact object, while the organizer impact page sends period and reads data.current and data.previous, so the page always shows its empty state and no impact figure is computed by any route.

GET /api/organizer/impact returns every organizer_tasks row of the organization to a steward or any role above: the low-role guard holds only callers below steward to their own member_id rows, so a steward reads the assignee, the member id, the related case and grievance ids, the blocked reason and the completion notes of every organizer task in the organization whatever case or grievance mandate the steward holds, and no read is audited.

POST /api/organizer/impact stores assigned_to, assigned_by, member_id, related_case_id and related_grievance_id from the body with no check that the assignee or member belongs to the organization or that the case and grievance exist in it (related_case_id and related_grievance_id are uuid columns with no foreign key), and status, completed_at and completion_notes are writable on creation, so a task can name a person, case or grievance of another organization and be created already completed.

GET /api/pension/retirement-eligibility is open at the member floor and selects every column of every pension_members row of the organization whose years_of_service is at or above a threshold taken from the query string (default 25, any value including 0 or a negative number is accepted), with no relation between the row and the caller, no administrator test and no pagination: any member receives the name, plan name, enrolment date, membership status, vesting status, years of service, organization membership id and metadata of every enrolled colleague, while the sibling benefits, contributions and T4A routes hold a non-administrator to their own records.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in member of an organization calls GET /api/pension/retirement-eligibility, optionally with threshold=0, and receives every pension_members row of the organization (name, plan name, enrolment date, membership status, years of service, vesting status, the organization membership id in user_id and the metadata JSON): the route filters only on the organization and the years of service and never relates a row to the caller.

potentialImpact.description: Colleagues learn who is enrolled in which pension plan, how many years each has served, whether each is vested, retired, deferred or terminated and how close each is to retirement, which the sibling pension routes now hold to the member own record or to the secretary-treasurer.

releaseDisposition.justification: The only guards are a session, an organization context and the member floor, the select returns every column of every enrolment row, and the threshold is a query value the caller sets, so a signed-in member reaches the personal pension standing of every enrolled colleague today; the sibling routes close exactly this read, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The route described as checking retirement eligibility applies no eligibility rule: it compares the administrator-typed years_of_service with a threshold that defaults to the literal 25 or is chosen by the caller, ignores age, plan type, vesting, membership status and plan terms, includes terminated, inactive and retired enrolments, and returns the matching rows as the members meeting eligibility; a NaN threshold is stringified into the comparison.

POST /api/pension/t4a is described as generating a T4A record but generates nothing: it inserts the memberId, memberName, taxYear and pensionIncome exactly as typed (pensionIncome is an unvalidated string, negative or non-numeric values reach the database), may store status generated and a caller-written generated date, derives the income from no contribution, benefit claim or payment, checks neither the member reference nor uniqueness per member and tax year, holds no slip number, box data or document, and transmits nothing to the tax authority, so the member reads an unsupported figure labelled generated as their tax record.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: The secretary-treasurer posts memberId, memberName, taxYear, pensionIncome and optionally status generated and a generated date; the route inserts the row exactly as typed in the tenant transaction, commits the pension.t4a.generate audit row and returns it, and the member reads it from GET /api/pension/t4a as their T4A record. The amount is not computed from any contribution, claim or payment and no slip document or box data exists.

potentialImpact.description: A record labelled generated that carries a hand-typed pension income, for a member id nobody verified and with no uniqueness per member and year, reaches the member as their tax record; if members or the organization rely on it for a return, the figure is unsupported by any pension payment record and the member is told a slip was generated when nothing was.

existingContainment.summary: Only the secretary_treasurer role can post, the status can only be draft or generated (never filed or amended), the insert carries the session organization and an atomic audit row commits with it, so a typed figure is attributable to one office and is never marked filed.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization records T4A rows with status generated for members and presents them, or lets members rely on them, as the tax slip of the year; the route then publishes unsupported tax figures as generated records.
releaseDisposition.justification: The reach is one named office and the status cannot claim a filing, so the harm needs the office to type a figure and a member to rely on the generated label; once pension payments are made and slips are issued from these rows, the unsourced amount and the absent generation step become a tax-record integrity failure that blocks release.

defectRegister.title: GET /api/pension/trustee-meetings and GET /api/pension/trustee-meetings/[id] require only the member floor and return every column of the meeting rows of the organization, including the agenda, the minutes text and the untyped attendees array, to every member: no role, trustee identity or decision names who may read the minutes of the pension trustees, the list is unbounded, and the trustee administration that would define a reader is not implemented.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in member calls GET /api/pension/trustee-meetings or /api/pension/trustee-meetings/<id> and receives every meeting row of the organization including its agenda, minutes and the untyped attendees array; the route filters on the organization only, and the secretary-treasurer writes the rows.

potentialImpact.description: The deliberations of the pension trustees (funding decisions, discussion of individual benefit cases and the names of attendees) reach every member of the organization with no decision about which members may read fiduciary minutes.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization records agenda items, minutes or an attendee list on a trustee meeting (the secretary-treasurer POST or PATCH); every member can then read that fiduciary record, which the institution has not decided to share.
releaseDisposition.justification: Nothing narrows the member-floor read, so the record is exposed to every member the moment it holds content; the harm needs the office to write minutes, which no source in the route prevents, so the defect blocks release for any organization that records trustee minutes.

defectRegister.title: PATCH and DELETE on /api/pension/trustee-meetings/[id] let the secretary_treasurer rewrite the minutes, agenda, attendees, date and status of a meeting that is already completed, or delete it permanently, with no state rule, no approval of the minutes, no version of the previous text and no trustee involvement; the audit row lists only the changed field names and the status or the title, so the previous minutes cannot be recovered or compared, and the attendees and minutes are unbounded untyped input.

The pension plan routes accept activeMembers, totalAssets and fundingStatus as typed values (fundingStatus and totalAssets are unvalidated strings written to numeric columns) and derive none of them from the pension_members, contribution or asset records, while GET /api/pension/plans and GET /api/pension/plans/[id] return every plan column, including those figures, the status and the metadata JSON, to any member of the organization, so a member reads plan assets and funding status that are whatever the administrator last typed, with no as-of date or source.

DELETE /api/pension/plans/[id] hard-deletes the pension_plans row for the secretary_treasurer with no check for the enrolments, contributions or claims of the plan (pension_members.plan_id has no foreign key, so the delete succeeds and the enrolments keep a plan id that no longer resolves), no state rule such as terminated, and an audit row that keeps only the plan name, so the funding figures and plan description of the deleted plan cannot be recovered from the audit record.

Creating, changing and deleting a plan, enrolling a member, recording a contribution, issuing a T4A record and keeping trustee meetings are all authorized by one role-title list (PENSION_ADMIN_ROLES is FINANCIAL_MEMBER_DATA_ROLES, the single role secretary_treasurer): no route requires a live financial mandate as the payroll routes do, none calls the kernel authorization, no second person approves, and the pension-authority source states that the trustee-administration authority is not implemented, so the fiduciary acts are one office acting alone on a role string.

The pension write routes store the member and plan references and the money as typed: contributions and T4A rows take memberId as any uuid, with memberName and amount as free strings that are not checked against the organization membership or the enrolment (amount may be negative or non-numeric), enrolment takes planId and userId as any uuid that need not exist or belong to the organization (the table has no foreign key) with yearsOfService, vesting and status typed, and a benefit claim takes memberName, claimType and amount as typed text with no plan, so the rows a member later reads as their own depend on the administrator entering the right identifier.

POST /api/pension/benefits files a claim as pending for any member who holds an organization membership (the claim is tied to no plan, no eligibility check and no amount limit), but no route in the application sets under_review, approved, denied or paid, no notification reaches a trustee or an administrator, and the route says the decision belongs to trustees that are not implemented, so every claim stays pending with no path to a decision and the member receives a filed claim that nothing will process.

None of the pension routes passes a rateLimit option to withApi, although lib/rate-limiter.ts defines PENSION_OPERATIONS for GET and POST /api/pension/* and nothing uses it, so the member own-record reads, the organization-wide administrator reads and the administration writes are limited only by whatever default the platform applies outside the route.

The pension list reads (benefits, contributions, T4A, members, plans, retirement eligibility and trustee meetings) return every matching row of the organization with no limit, offset or page, so an administrator read of a large organization, or the member-floor reads of plans, meetings and eligibility, returns the whole table in one response.

GET /api/pension/members is described as listing the pension members of the organization by plan, but it adds a condition that pension_members.user_id equals the caller organization membership id for every caller including the secretary_treasurer, so the administration console that calls it with a plan id to list that plan members receives only the administrator own enrolment (the member console relies on the same own-enrolment answer to find the member pension id); the description and the administrator use do not match the behaviour.

The member-floor pension reads (members, plans, plan item, retirement eligibility, trustee meetings and the meeting item) query through the shared db import and only the explicit organization predicate scopes them: the row-level-security context is set by withApi only when rlsOrgContext is set or the canonical state context is enabled, so outside that mode the policy that the pension tables carry is not what isolates the tenant and the single where clause is the whole boundary, unlike the own-record reads and the writes that open withRLSContext.

The /api/portal/documents and /api/portal/documents/upload routes are the same crudRoutes configuration over cms_pages (readRole member, writeRole steward, orgScoped true) with no handler of their own: no portal principal or member identity is read, the list is not scoped to documents addressed to the caller, and the two files are byte-identical, so the upload path lists and creates the same page rows as the collection path.

GET on the portal document routes returns cms_pages rows of every status (draft, review, scheduled, published, archived) and every column to any member, including the author user id, the file URL and the content JSON, and never applies the requires_auth and allowed_roles columns of the row, so a document restricted to officers in its own row is listed to every member; pages hold at most 100 rows.

POST /api/portal/documents/upload (and POST /api/portal/documents) copies the request body into a cms_pages insert: no multipart file is read, no file type or size is validated, no malware scan runs, no storage key is derived under the organization, and file_url, content_type and file_size_mb are whatever strings and numbers the steward typed (any URL scheme, any size), so the route reports an upload as created while nothing was received or stored and the row can point members at an arbitrary external or script URL; the file-receiving route /api/documents/upload that validates, scans and stores is not called.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A steward posts any JSON body to /api/portal/documents/upload and the generic factory inserts a cms_pages row with the stored fileUrl, contentType, fileSizeMb, status and role columns exactly as sent and returns it; no file is received, typed, sized, scanned or stored under an organization key, so the success reply for an upload describes only a row that points at a string.

potentialImpact.description: A caller or a screen that believes the route stores a member document is told it did, while the row can name any external or internal URL as the document; a published row is then offered to members as a document without a type, size or malware check and with no storage owned by the organization.

existingContainment.summary: Only a steward or above can post, the factory sets the session organization and the author on the row, and the insert commits with a crud.cms_pages.create audit record that names the fields written.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: A client, integration or portal screen submits member documents to /api/portal/documents/upload, or a member screen renders cms_pages file_url values as downloadable documents; the route then reports an upload that never happened and offers unscanned URLs to members.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route is reachable by stewards and records an attributable row, so the harm needs something to treat it as the upload endpoint or to render its URL; the real file-receiving route is separate, and once a screen relies on this path the reply is an unsupported success with no file controls, so the condition blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The portal document POST inserts any cms_pages column from the body at the steward floor, including status published, published_at, requires_auth, allowed_roles, view_count and download_count, whereas the content status route moves a row from draft to review only for a content_manager and from review to published only for an administrator under a row lock; a steward therefore creates a published document with no review and no administrator step, and the role that publishes through the workflow is not the role that publishes here.

The commercial transition route lets one platform-tier administrator move a pilot application through contract_sent, contract_signed, invoice_issued and subscription_active, and it inserts a commercial contract (pending_approval, then set to active with signedAt the moment contract_signed is posted, with no signature, acceptance or counterpart step), a platform invoice with status issued for the approved pilot amount and an active organization subscription for the verified organization, while a pilot status of approved, active or completed is written from the state alone; when the billing account, the draft contract or the plan is missing the route only pushes a note that the effect was staged (for example No billing account found; monetization side effects were staged only) and still commits the new commercial state, status, score history and an atomic audit row that names the target state, so the record, the response and the history say the contract was signed or the invoice issued when no contract, invoice or subscription row was written.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Only a caller whose resolved role is at or above the system_admin level can post a transition, and the application must already be bound to an organization and, for the contract, invoice and subscription states, carry terms approved by a second administrator; within that set a single administrator can mark a contract signed and issue an invoice to the bound organization without any acceptance by that organization.

potentialImpact.description: An organization could be invoiced and shown as holding an active contract or subscription that it never accepted, and the commercial state, pilot status and audit trail would state a signature and outcome that no counterpart gave, or state a signed or issued step when only a note was staged and nothing was written.

existingContainment.summary: The route refuses callers below the system_admin level, refuses an application whose organization is not bound, requires approved commercial terms (approved by an administrator other than the one who bound the organization) before any financial state, and commits the effects with an atomic audit row in one transaction.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The platform operator uses the transition route to issue a pilot contract, invoice or subscription to an organization, or a contract state or an issued or active record is relied on as evidence that the organization accepted the terms.
releaseDisposition.justification: The harm needs an operator to run the financial states against a real organization, which the role floor and the two-administrator terms approval limit to a small actor set, so the route is not open to every caller; but nothing in the route or the schema records that the counterpart accepted a contract or an invoice, and a missing billing account still advances the recorded state, so the route must not be used to issue financial artifacts to an organization until an acceptance step and an honest staged outcome exist.

defectRegister.title: The pilot platform tier (applications list, verify-organization, rebind-organization, approve-commercial-terms, commercial-transition and the cross-organization branch of every per-application route) is decided by hasMinRole(system_admin) and by an actor level at or above PILOT_PLATFORM_ACCESS_MIN_LEVEL, which is ROLE_HIERARCHY.system_admin (200), and the hierarchy places platform staff titles such as support_agent (218) and data_analyst (215) above that level, so any account whose resolved role title is one of those titles, or whose user id is in PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS in the legacy mode, passes every platform check and may read every application with the contact details, bind it to any organization and approve terms; the gate is a role title and no platform-staff mandate or kernel decision backs it.

Before a platform administrator binds an application, the effective owner is responses.organizationId, a value the anonymous applicant typed into the public form (the only reserved key sanitizeResponsesForPublicCreate leaves in place), so an applicant can name any organization id and thereby decide whose stewards pass the same-organization check on the item routes (read, PATCH of non-reserved fields including readinessScore, memberCount and the organization and contact fields, and the artifact, intelligence and reference-profile writes), which lets a submitter place an application and its generated content in the workspace of an organization that never received it.

The public application route buckets its only abuse control, 5 submissions per hour, on the first comma-separated value of the x-forwarded-for header, then x-real-ip, then the literal unknown, and no bot challenge, e-mail proof or captcha is read, so wherever the platform edge does not overwrite that header a caller can send a new value with every request and submit without bound, each submission also creating a HubSpot contact and deal; the limiter fails closed only when Redis is unavailable.

After the insert the public application route awaits upsertContact and createDeal, which send the typed contact name, e-mail address, phone number, organization name, member count and organization type and a deal named for the organization to HubSpot whenever HUBSPOT_API_KEY is set, for any syntactically valid address the submitter typed, with no proof that the submitter controls it, no consent text stored or shown and no decision naming who may receive the contact; the submitter response does not say that the contact is shared.

The public application schema bounds every named field but accepts responses as z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) and assessment as a passthrough object, with no key count, depth or serialized size limit, and stores responses (minus the reserved keys other than organizationId) in a JSONB column that every later read, proposal, timeline and export returns, so an anonymous submitter can store an arbitrarily large document that the platform-tier list and all per-application reads must serialize.

The proposal, artifact version, package export, reference profile and commercial transition outputs state adoption, activity, champion and risk scores, a renewal and expansion likelihood, an opportunity tier and a qualification, all computed by calculateCommercialSignals and the qualification functions from readinessScore (the applicant self-assessment, typed on the public form or amended by a steward PATCH, and treated as 55 when absent), the stage the administrator reached in the commercial sequence, and memberCount, with championScore and activityScore taken from responses keys that no route writes, so the figures read as measured pilot customer success signals when no pilot activity is an input.

The verify-organization route binds a pilot application to the organization id in the body after bindPilotOrganization checks only that an organizations row with that id exists and that the application is not bound to a different one, and then stamps verifiedBy and verifiedAt; no applicant e-mail domain, contact membership, document or other proof that the applicant belongs to or speaks for the organization is compared or recorded, no reason is required, and the audit row is written under the target organization, so the field named verified states an administrator selection and not a verification.

The approve-commercial-terms route stores the member count as typed by the administrator, an optional subscription plan and a pilot amount that is either the typed number (any value from 0.01 to 9999999999.99) or the lower bound of a price band, as verifiedMemberCount, verifiedPilotAmount and verifiedSubscriptionPlanId on the application with the approver and time, and these values later become the contract value, invoice total and subscription; the only second-person control is that the approver differs from the administrator who bound the organization, no source for the member count or the amount is recorded, and no representative of the applicant organization accepts the terms.

The commercial transition, artifacts, intelligence and reference-profile POST handlers cast request.json() to a TypeScript type with no schema, and persist the caller strings (reason, source, notes, milestone, lessonLearned, objectionRaised, requestedFeature, deploymentBlocker, stakeholder and note) with no length bound into the responses JSONB column and, for the transition, into the audit details; the intelligence handler appends to arrays on every call, so a steward of the claimed organization or a platform-tier actor can grow the column without limit and every later read, proposal and timeline serializes it.

The artifacts, intelligence and reference-profile POST handlers write through withLockedPilotMutation, which locks the application and merges the response keys with a single UPDATE and writes no audit row, and the routes write none, so a steward of the claimed organization or a platform-tier actor can add artifact versions, intelligence notes (lessons, objections, requested features, blockers and stakeholder sentiment) and reference snapshots to a pilot application with no durable record of who did so, although the coverage manifest declares these writes atomically audited.

The reference profile route builds a testimonial, a case study and a benchmark dataset for a pilot application where the testimonial quote is a response key a steward or the applicant can set (referenceTestimonialQuote, authored and role keys are not reserved) or else the literal text that the organization established a repeatable pilot operating cadence with measurable adoption growth, attributed to the application contact name with the role Pilot Sponsor, the time saved is Math.max(6, Math.round(adoptionRate * 0.18)) hours a week (never below 6), and adoption, engagement and health come from a pilot_metrics row or else from the synthetic proposal signals and a 100 minus risk figure; the case study titled as 90-day pilot outcomes and the benchmark record are persisted by POST as a versioned snapshot with a checksum, so quoted words, hours saved and outcomes that no pilot customer said or measured are stored as reference material for the organization with no attestation or consent step.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A steward of the organization an application claims, or a platform-tier actor, can read the generated reference profile and persist it as a versioned snapshot; the output is returned to that caller and stored in the application, and no route, page or message in the repository publishes it to a third party.

potentialImpact.description: A fabricated testimonial in a named contact words, an invented hours-saved figure and score-derived adoption and health numbers would be presented as pilot outcomes and, if used in a case study or benchmark, would state customer results and a quotation that no customer gave or consented to.

existingContainment.summary: The routes require the steward floor and the ownership check, the snapshot is stored in the application row and returned only to the authorized caller, and the repository contains no caller that sends the profile, case study or benchmark dataset outside the organization.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The generated reference profile, case study or benchmark dataset is shown to a prospect, published, attached to a proposal or sent outside the organization, or a customer-facing page is built that reads the stored reference versions.
releaseDisposition.justification: The output is invented in part and stored as a case study, but it stays inside the application row and the authorized caller today, so the impact needs a publication step that no code takes; the testimonial text and hours-saved figure are not measured or attested and must not be shown to a third party as a customer result until a customer attestation and consent step exist.

defectRegister.title: The champions, friction, metrics and conversion-assessment routes (admin floor) read the organization from the organizationId query parameter and never compare it with the session organization, then call services that run raw SQL over pilot_events through the bare db import filtered only by that id, returning per-user ids with case, update and active-day counts (champions), user ids with the date of the last login or case (friction, full report), unique-user, case and update counts with a daily active user trend (metrics) and the counts that decide a conversion flag (readiness); an administrator of any organization can therefore read the usage telemetry of any organization whose id they know, and the only boundary left is a row-level-security policy that applies only when the request runs under the canonical tenant context.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator of any organization can request champions, friction, metrics or conversion figures for any organization id; in the canonical bootstrap mode the wrapper opens a tenant transaction for the caller organization so the pilot_events policy hides the other organization rows, and in the legacy mode nothing opens a tenant transaction so the queries run on the pool connection with only the explicit id predicate.

potentialImpact.description: Where the connection is not constrained by the pilot_events policy, an administrator of one organization would read another organization member user ids with case and update counts, last login dates, unique-user counts, daily active user trend and conversion readiness counts, which is another union activity data and personal behavioural data the caller session does not entitle them to.

existingContainment.summary: In the canonical bootstrap mode withApiAuth runs the handler inside withRLSContext for the caller organization and the pilot_events table carries a direct organization policy, so a query for another organization finds no rows; the deployment descriptor for the production container app sets that mode.

releaseDisposition.justification: The routes themselves enforce nothing about whose organization is named, any administrator of any organization reaches them and the data is per-user behavioural telemetry from another tenant; the confinement rests on a row-level policy that applies only under the canonical bootstrap mode, which the code treats as off by default and the pilot environment descriptor does not set, so the cross-tenant read is reachable as the application is written and the pilot environment is a place it is not contained.

defectRegister.title: The pilot events route lets any member write a pilot_events row of any of 25 event types (including case_created, update_added, first_case_created, org_created, user_invited and role_assigned) with an unbounded metadata object, through a bare-db insert with no audit, and for case_created and update_added only reads metadata.caseId without checking that the case exists or belongs to the organization; the champion detection (3 cases, 5 updates, 5 active days), the conversion readiness flag (3 active users in 14 days, 10 cases, 5 updates, 5 active days), the friction lists and the engagement metrics are computed purely from these rows, so a member can make an organization appear to hold champions and a conversion-ready pilot without creating a case.

The CUPE bootstrap route (system_admin floor, allowed when NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo) resolves the target organization by the slug in a fixture file (cupe-local-123) and, when the body sets reset, deletes every grievance, every organization_members row and every pilot_checklist_items row of that organization with predicates on the organization id alone, with no demo marker, row-origin check, dry run, confirmation or backup, and then re-inserts fixture members (including roles such as admin and president under fixed fixture user ids) and grievances with onConflictDoNothing, so if the organization at that slug holds real grievances or members in a pilot or demo runtime the reset destroys them and the audit row records only the counts the fixture attempted.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A caller at or above the system_admin level, in a runtime whose NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo, can reset the organization found at the fixture slug; the pilot and the CUPE demo environment descriptors both set those modes, and the route is rate limited and writes an atomic audit row.

potentialImpact.description: Real grievance records, member rows and checklist state of the organization that owns the slug would be hard-deleted without recovery by one request, and fixture members with elevated organization roles would be seeded under user ids that are literal strings in the repository.

existingContainment.summary: The route requires the system_admin level, refuses unless NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo, takes the slug from a repository fixture and not from the request, applies a write rate limit and writes an atomic audit row for the reset.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The organization at the fixture slug holds records that were not created by the bootstrap in a runtime whose NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo, or the bootstrap is run against a pilot environment that serves a real organization.
releaseDisposition.justification: The reset is an operator action behind a role floor and a runtime mode gate, and the slug is fixed, so an arbitrary organization cannot be named; but the delete predicate is the organization id alone and the pilot mode is the mode of the real pilot deployment, so the data loss is real wherever the slug belongs to a live organization, and the route cannot tell seeded rows from real ones.

defectRegister.title: The CUPE bootstrap response reports seeded.worksites as the number of worksites in the fixture although the handler never inserts a worksite, increments membersInserted and casesInserted once per attempted insert even when onConflictDoNothing skipped the row, and returns onboarding checklistInitialized, completed 3 and pending 2 as literals for five checklist ids (org_profile_configured, team_invited, first_case_created, sla_watchdog_enabled and billing_connected) while the onboarding route reads and toggles only seven different ids (org-seeded, users-invited and others), so the seeded rows are never shown by the checklist route, a toggle of a seeded id answers 404, and the same literals and counts are written into the audit details.

The demo-data route (officer floor, pilot or demo runtime) inserts four employers named for real federal departments with e-mail addresses on real government domains (lr-demo@tbs-sct.gc.ca and others) and fictional grievances with named grievants into the employers and grievances tables of the officer organization, the same tables that hold real records, with no demo marker column on either row (only a GRV-DEMO- number prefix and an lr-demo@ address prefix), so the seeded cases are counted as cases managed by the pilot metrics and listed with real grievances, and the purge deletes every row of the organization whose grievance number starts with GRV-DEMO- or whose employer e-mail starts with lr-demo@ whether or not the seed created it.

The pilot current and overview routes report organizerAdoptionRate and memberEngagementRate as the share of organization_members rows whose updated_at falls in the last 30 days (any edit of the row counts as activity), report avgTimeToResolution as the mean of COALESCE(resolved_at, NOW()) minus created_at over grievances created in the last 30 days, so an unresolved case counts as resolved at the moment of the request, count seeded demo grievances in casesManaged, and replace a figure with the stored pilot_enrollments value when no live row exists, with no indication in the response that the figure is a proxy or a stored fallback.

The onboarding checklist PATCH lets any officer mark any of seven steps (contracts-uploaded, employers-imported, integrations-configured, export-verified and others) completed or reopened with a boolean in the body and stamps completedBy and completedAt, and writes a pilot.checklist_completed audit row when all seven are true, without checking that a contract was uploaded, employers were imported, an integration was configured or an export was verified, so the checklist state, isComplete flag and audit trail record asserted steps.

The pilot overview route (officer floor) admits a platform administrator identity or, in the legacy mode, any member of the platform organization (DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID) holding the officer role title, then under withSystemContext lists every actively enrolled organization with its id, name, slug, enrollment date, adoption and engagement rates, cases managed, resolution time, health score and milestones, running three queries for each enrollment and with no pagination, so the cross-organization aggregate is reachable by an officer role title of one organization and no platform-staff mandate or read audit exists.

The pilot current route resolves the session organization with withOrganizationAuth and then runs its enrollment, milestone, member and grievance reads inside withSystemContext, so the row-level policies that scope pilot_enrollments, pilot_milestones, organization_members and grievances to the caller organization do not apply and the explicit eq(organizationId) and the interpolated organization id in the two SQL statements are the only scope.

The pilot feedback POST validates easeRating, category and trigger but passes comment from the body unvalidated and unbounded (any JSON value, no length limit) into pilot_feedback.comment, and the administrator GET returns the ten most recent rows with select() including userId and the raw comment to any administrator of the organization, so free text and the identity of the member who wrote it are returned without a length bound or an anonymity decision.

GET /api/organizations checks only that a session user id exists, applies no role floor and no organization predicate of its own (the only filters are the optional parent and status query parameters), and selects every organizations row visible to the connection inside withRLSContext: in the legacy mode that transaction only sets app.current_org_id and never switches to the union_eyes_runtime role, so whether the list is confined to the caller organization depends on the database role of the connection, and where it is not, any signed-in user receives every organization with its contact email, phone, website, address, charter number, subscription tier, billing contact id, settings JSON, enabled features, member counts, creator id and legacy id, and with include_stats the active grievance count of each listed organization.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in user calls /api/organizations (optionally with parent, status and include_stats): the handler authenticates the session user, opens withRLSContext and returns every organizations row the connection role lets the 0108 policy show, mapped with billing contact id, settings, enabled features, contact fields and member counts, and the per-organization active grievance counts when include_stats is true.

potentialImpact.description: A member of one organization can read the commercial, billing-contact and configuration data of other organizations, and the number of open grievances each has, when the connection role is not confined by the organizations row-level-security policy; an ordinary member of the own organization receives the billing contact and settings JSON in every case.

existingContainment.summary: In the canonical mode (UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 set to 1) withRLSContext switches the transaction to the union_eyes_runtime role so the 0108 policy (a tenant sees only its own organization row) confines the list to the caller organization; the legacy transaction has no such switch.

evidence.quote: SELECT ue_create_direct_org_rls_policy('organizations', 'id', FALSE); -- a tenant sees only its own org row

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The deployment runs with UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 unset or 0 and the DATABASE_URL role used by the shared db client is not confined by the 0108 organizations policy, so the list returns organizations other than the caller own.
releaseDisposition.justification: The canonical mode confines the read to the caller organization row, so the cross-tenant exposure exists only in the legacy mode and only if the connection role is not bound by the policy; both are runtime facts the route does not state. Where both hold, any signed-in user receives the commercial and configuration data of every organization, so the route blocks release under that condition, and the own-organization over-disclosure is recorded separately by the earlier current-organization defect.

defectRegister.title: GET /api/organizations returns whatever the tenant context lets the policy show while three administration pages (the new organization page, the edit organization page and the members console) treat the answer as the list of organizations of the union for choosing a parent or an organization: under a connection confined by the 0108 policy the list is the caller own row only, so the parent picker is empty of any other organization and the parent query parameter finds no children, and under an unconfined connection it is every organization (the exposure of DEF-0B10-OPL-01); the route also applies no limit, passes the parent query string to a uuid column unvalidated so that a malformed value raises an unhandled database error and a 500, and lets withRLSContext throw an unhandled error (500) for a user with no selected organization.

POST /api/organizations is limited to a system administrator and commits the organization row and its organization.create audit row in one system transaction, but it reads the body with no schema and no guard on the JSON parse (a malformed body raises an unhandled error and a 500) and writes whatever the body states: name and slug are not checked (a missing name or a duplicate slug surfaces as an unhandled database error), the cached member_count and active_member_count counters, status, settings JSON, enabled features and CLC affiliation are taken from the body, and the parent may be any organization (the parent is only checked to exist, not for its status or its type, and the administrators of the parent have no say in a new child attached to it), so one request can create an organization with invented member counts under any parent of the hierarchy.

POST /api/organizations inserts only name, slug, display_name, type, parent, sectors, email, phone, website, status, CLC affiliation, member counters, settings and features: the description that the new organization page sends is dropped and the sector and jurisdiction that the page sends are stored only inside the settings JSON (the sectors and province_territory columns stay empty), the organization hierarchy admin component sends the type local_union, which the handler refuses with 400, and then tests data.success, a field the handler never returns, so a created organization is not shown and a refused one is not reported; the handler answers 201 with the stored row while the data the caller entered is partly absent from it.

GET /api/organizations/search checks only that a session user id exists and then runs the search inside withSystemContext (the union_eyes_system role that the 0108 policy for the organizations table exempts) with no membership, role or mandate check: any signed-in user can match organizations of every tenant by name or slug (a search with no q returns up to 50 organizations other than the platform type) and receives the id, name, slug, type, parent id, member count, status and sectors of each, so the directory discloses the size, lifecycle status and place in the parent and child hierarchy of organizations the caller has no relationship with.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in user calls /api/organizations/search?q=<text> (or with no q): the handler checks only the session user id, reads the organizations table with the system role and returns the id, name, slug, type, parent id, member count, status and sectors of up to 50 organizations of any tenant.

potentialImpact.description: A member of one organization can enumerate other organizations, learn their member counts, lifecycle status and parent affiliation, and walk the hierarchy by parent id, which the 0108 row-level-security policy states a tenant must not see and which the directory-visibility decision has not authorized.

releaseDisposition.justification: The only check is a session user id; the read deliberately runs with the system role that bypasses the tenant policy and returns size, status and parent fields beyond a name directory, so a signed-in user of any organization reaches directory data of every other organization and the route blocks release until the visible fields and the readers are decided.

defectRegister.title: GET /api/organizations/search excludes the platform organization type only when no q is given: with a q the filter is an ILIKE on name or slug that returns organizations of every type and every lifecycle status (platform, archived, suspended and inactive organizations included), the q is placed unescaped inside the pattern (a percent sign or underscore matches every row) with no minimum length, the result is limited to 50 with no ordering, no paging and no signal that it was cut, and the statement selects every column of the organizations row (billing contact, settings, contacts) although the mapper returns eight of them.

When the canonical bootstrap flag is not 1, GET /api/organizations/tree checks only that a session user exists and then reads every organization, with no limit and no filter on type or status (platform, archived, suspended and inactive organizations included), through the shared db client with no withRLSContext, no withSystemContext, no membership check and no comparison with the caller organization, and returns the id, name, slug, type, parent id, sector, jurisdiction, description, hierarchy level, member count, status and timestamps of each: the whole parent and child hierarchy of the union is treated as visible to every signed-in user, and whether the result is confined to the caller depends entirely on the row-level-security role of the connection (a confined connection with no organization context returns an empty tree for everyone); only the canonical branch limits the tree to the active private memberships of the caller.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in user loads the organization context in the legacy mode: the client calls /api/organizations/tree, the handler authenticates the session user and returns every organization the shared db client can read, with parent id, hierarchy level, member count, sector, jurisdiction and description, with no membership check.

potentialImpact.description: A member of one organization can read the identity, size, jurisdiction, description and parent affiliation of every organization of the union whenever the connection role is not confined by the organizations row-level-security policy, and a tree of the whole hierarchy is treated as visible because the organizations are related by parent and child, which is not an authorization to read them.

existingContainment.summary: In the canonical mode (UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 set to 1) the route returns getCanonicalOrganizationTree, which lists only the active organizations of the private memberships of the caller; the legacy branch has no such limit.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The deployment runs with UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 unset or 0 and the DATABASE_URL role used by the shared db client is not confined by the 0108 organizations policy, so the legacy branch returns organizations other than the caller own.
releaseDisposition.justification: The canonical branch is membership scoped, so the exposure exists only in the legacy mode and only if the connection role is not bound by the policy; both are runtime facts the route does not state. Where both hold the route discloses every tenant organization to any signed-in user, so it blocks release under that condition.

defectRegister.title: The legacy branches of GET /api/organizations/tree and POST /api/organizations/switch fill missing values with invented ones: in both a null created_at or updated_at is replaced by the time of the request and a null type becomes union, and the tree also turns a null status into active, a null hierarchy level into 0 and a null member count into 0, so the caller reads a creation date, a type, a lifecycle status and a size that the organization record does not hold.

In the legacy mode POST /api/organizations/switch accepts any organization_members row of the user and the organization as the membership (it reads neither the status nor the removal flag of the row, and does not check that the organization is active), so a suspended, inactive or removed member and a member of an archived organization receive success true together with the organization name, slug, type, parent id, sector, jurisdiction and description, although the organization resolver that later reads the selection cookie requires an active, non-removed membership; an identifier on the PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS environment list switches to any organization without any membership; and the route stores nothing server side (the client then writes the selection into cookies it controls), so success true reports a validation and not a switch.

POST /api/organizations/switch changes the organization a session works in (the canonical mode revokes the active session and issues a new session row bound to the chosen organization, or writes a provider preference cookie) and neither the route, the canonical selection handler nor rebindSessionOrganization writes an audit record of who selected which organization from which, so the selection of an organization, including a platform administrator selecting an organization they hold no membership of in the legacy mode, leaves no audit trail and the mutation of the session store is not atomic with any audit record.

GET /api/organizations/platform-id returns the constant DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID of the source file as platformOrgId without reading the organizations table: the constant is documented in organization-utils as the Default Organization where all users start (the organization that the non-production fallback assigns to a user with no membership), not as the organization of type platform, so a client that distinguishes viewing the platform from viewing a tenant (the sidebar compares the organization id with this same constant) treats the default tenant organization as the platform, and every signed-in user receives the internal identifier of that organization.

GET /api/platform/metrics/mrr, GET /api/platform/metrics/churn and GET /api/platform/metrics/unit-economics are three copies of one handler that ignores the request, reads no table and returns the fixed object activeUsers 0, requestsToday 0, errorRate 0 under the OpenAPI summary System metrics: a caller that asks for monthly recurring revenue, churn or unit economics receives zeros for three system-usage keys that are none of those figures (no mrr, churn or unit-economics key exists), presented with HTTP 200 as aggregated system metrics, although the subscription event, MRR snapshot and customer acquisition tables exist in the financial service schema and no route under app/api reads them.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator of any organization calls /api/platform/metrics/mrr, /churn or /unit-economics and receives 200 with activeUsers 0, requestsToday 0 and errorRate 0; no figure is read from any table, so the response reads as zero users, zero requests and a zero error rate for the platform whatever the subscriptions are.

potentialImpact.description: A dashboard, report or investor or board summary that reads these paths as revenue, churn or unit-economics figures would record zero recurring revenue, zero churn and no cost per customer as measured facts of the platform, and an operator would read an absent measurement as a healthy or an empty business.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: Any client, report, dashboard or integration reads one of the three paths as a revenue, churn or unit-economics figure (the application source has no caller today), or the paths are advertised as the platform revenue metrics.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route returns a fixed object of zeros with a success status under a path that names a financial measure, with no containment that marks the figure as unmeasured; it harms only when a consumer reads it as a measurement, which the source does not show today, so it blocks release once the paths are consumed or advertised.

defectRegister.title: The three platform metric routes under /api/platform/metrics are gated at the admin role floor (the organization administrator level of ROLE_HIERARCHY, 140) while the other platform-wide reads (the platform statistics and the platform operator routes) use the platform_lead floor (270): a route of the platform namespace that is wired to the platform revenue tables (mrr_snapshots has no organization column and subscription_events holds the events of every organization) would hand platform-wide revenue and churn aggregates to the administrator of every organization, and the route is a role-title check with no platform-staff mandate.

GET /api/platform/stats admits any caller whose role title is platform_lead or above (a role-title floor, not an issued platform-staff mandate) and returns, for every organization other than the platform type, an organization list with name, type, status, member and active member counts, sectors, CLC affiliation, subscription tier and per-capita rate, together with registered and active user counts, role distribution, grievance, collective agreement and settlement counts, the total monetary value of all settlements and the sector breakdown: the statements run on the shared db client with no organization predicate, no withSystemContext and no withRLSContext (so whether they see every tenant depends on the connection role) and the read is not audited.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A caller holding the platform_lead role title or above (the operations dashboard calls the route) receives platform-wide figures: per-organization subscription tier, per-capita rate, member counts and lifecycle status, grievance and settlement totals over all organizations, and the distribution of roles of all members; no platform-staff mandate is checked and no audit record is written for the read.

potentialImpact.description: Commercial and operational data of every organization is read by whoever holds the platform_lead role title, with no recorded mandate, scope, expiry or read audit, and the settlement and grievance totals aggregate the records of all tenants; if a role of that title is held outside the platform staff or the connection is unconfined, one account reads the commercial position of every union.

existingContainment.summary: The route requires the platform_lead role floor (level 270, above the organization administrator level), which limits the actor set to platform operations roles, but the title is not a mandate and the read is neither scoped nor audited.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: A platform_lead (or higher) role is held by any person the institution has not issued a platform-staff mandate to, which the open decision on the platform-staff mandate leaves undetermined for every operator account, or the route is exposed to a customer-facing client.
releaseDisposition.justification: The role floor limits the actors to platform operations roles, so the read is not open to tenant members, but the institution has not decided who may read across organizations and the read has no mandate, scope or audit; the disclosure of every organization commercial and operational data to a role title blocks release as soon as any operator account holds that title without a mandate.

defectRegister.title: The figures of GET /api/platform/stats are named for something other than what is computed: registeredUsers is the count of organization_members rows (one person with several memberships counts several times and removed members are not excluded) and activeUsers is the count of rows whose status is active, totalMonetaryValue is the sum of the integer monetary_amount of every settlement in every status (proposed and rejected settlements included, in no stated currency), and resolved grievances are only those with status settled; the dashboard shows these under labels of users, settlement value and resolved cases, so a count of rows and a sum of unaccepted amounts read as measured facts.

GET /api/portal/dues/balance reads the organization id from the organizationId query value or the x-organization-id header and queries member_dues_ledger through the shared db import with the session user id and that organization id as its only predicates: it does not verify that the caller is a member of the named organization (the sibling pay GET does), opens no withRLSContext, and returns totals and the last five entries, so the answer is bounded only by the user id predicate and by whatever row-level-security the connection role enforces.

The balanceStatus of GET /api/portal/dues/balance is computed as currentBalance <= 0 ? paid_up : currentBalance > 0 ? owing : credit, so the credit branch can never be returned: a member whose balance is negative (overpaid) is reported as paid_up and the credit they hold is not distinguished from a zero balance.

GET /api/portal/dues/pay is described as the member payment history but selects every transaction type of the member dues ledger (charges, credits, adjustments, write-offs and payments) under the key payments, includes the processor payment reference and receipt number, never lists the pending dues_transactions attempts that POST creates, and takes the page size from parseInt of the query value, so a non-numeric limit becomes NaN and the query limit is undefined.

POST /api/portal/dues/pay computes the outstanding balance, inserts a new pending dues_transactions row for the whole balance and creates a Stripe PaymentIntent with an idempotency key derived from that new row id, without looking for an existing pending payment of the member, so every call creates another full-balance intent; the settlement path locks and settles only the paid row and credits member_dues_ledger by that row amount (balance_after is the prior balance minus the amount, with no floor and no comparison with the balance owed), so two confirmed intents credit the ledger twice.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: When UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1 a member who calls POST /api/portal/dues/pay repeatedly (a double click, a retry after a timeout, two tabs) gets a new pending dues_transactions row and a new Stripe PaymentIntent for the full outstanding balance on each call, because the idempotency key is derived from the new payment id and no existing pending payment is looked up; settlement locks only the paid row and credits the ledger by that row amount without comparing it with the balance then owed.

potentialImpact.description: A member who confirms two of the intents is charged twice for the same dues and the ledger is credited twice, driving the balance below zero (balance_after is the prior balance minus the amount with no floor), so money is taken from a member beyond what they owe and the union carries a refund that no route can issue.

existingContainment.summary: The initiation answers 501 unless the deployment sets UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1, and settlement of a payment is a single guarded update from pending, so a given pending payment cannot settle twice.

evidence.quote: throw ApiError.notImplemented('Member dues payment is not enabled in this deployment')

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: A deployment sets UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1 so that members can pay dues through the application; the route then creates one charge-capable intent per call for the entire balance and can collect the same dues more than once.
releaseDisposition.justification: The flag keeps the route at 501 today, so no member can be charged now, but the defect is in the initiation and settlement logic and not in a configuration choice: the moment the flag is enabled every repeat call yields another full-balance intent and nothing in the settlement path stops the second payment from crediting the ledger past zero, so enabling member dues payments is blocked until the repeat and overpayment paths are closed.

defectRegister.title: POST /api/portal/dues/pay commits the pending dues_transactions row and its dues.payment_initiated audit row in one transaction and only then calls the Stripe API outside any transaction; the later update that stores processor_payment_id and the update that sets the row to cancelled after a processor failure are separate transactions with no audit row, and the cancellation is wrapped in a catch that discards its own failure, so an initiation can be audited for a payment whose provider call never happened and the cancelled state is not audited.

POST /api/portal/dues/pay sends the organization id and the member user id in the PaymentIntent metadata to Stripe through the platform-managed Stripe client (lib/stripe delegates to a platform client; the route holds no per-organization processor configuration): no source names the merchant account that receives union dues, whether it is the union or the platform operator, or the member consent for the disclosure, and the route holds no per-organization processor configuration.

The generic CRUD routes at /api/precedents/[id] are configured orgScoped true over arbitration_precedents, whose organization column is named source_organization_id and which has no organizationId, no status and no userId or memberId: the factory adds the tenant predicate only for an organizationId column and the low-role guard holds a caller to own rows only for a userId or memberId column, so GET (member), PATCH (steward) and DELETE (administrator) address any precedent row of any organization by id, whatever its sharing_level and shared_with_org_ids.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A member of any organization can GET, a steward can PATCH and an administrator can DELETE /api/precedents/<id> for any arbitration_precedents row: orgScoped true adds a tenant predicate only when the table has an organization column, and this table is keyed by source_organization_id, so the factory query filters on the id alone and the low-role guard finds no owner column to hold a member to.

potentialImpact.description: A precedent another organization contributed, whatever its sharing level (the column defaults to federation and the sector statistics treat private as excluded), is readable, rewritable (including its sharing level, shared-with list, document links and source organization) and permanently deletable with its tags and citations by users of other organizations once its id is known.

releaseDisposition.justification: The route has no tenant predicate and no sharing test, the table carries a sharing level and a shared-with list that no read or write route applies, and a row-level-security policy on source_organization_id applies only on a connection role that is subject to it, which the source does not establish for these reads and writes; a cross-tenant read and write of institutional case material is not contained by that, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: PATCH /api/precedents/[id] copies the request body into the arbitration_precedents update, so a steward can change sharing_level, shared_with_org_ids, is_parties_anonymized (turning the anonymization of the parties off), the document links and the source_organization_id itself with no sharing authority, no review and no record of the previous value; the audit row lists only the changed field names.

DELETE /api/precedents/[id] permanently deletes the arbitration_precedents row (the table has no status column, so the factory hard-deletes) and the foreign keys on precedent_tags and precedent_citations cascade, so the tags and the citation history of the precedent are destroyed with no soft delete, no withdrawal rule and an audit row that keeps only the row id and the changed field names.

GET /api/precedents (list, issue type, most cited) and POST /api/precedents/search select every column of arbitration_decisions at the member and steward floor, including the grievor name, the panel members, the full text and the embedding, and apply no condition on is_public or access_restrictions, so a decision recorded as not public or carrying an access restriction is returned and searched (the search also matches inside the full text) exactly like a public one; the table has no organization column and the library is shared across organizations.

GET /api/precedents passes parseInt of the limit and page query values to the list, most-cited and issue-type queries with no maximum, no minimum and no NaN check, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large page, a negative offset or a NaN limit, and the sortBy value is taken from the query string; the statistics mode counts the whole library.

POST /api/precedents/search validates only that the query is a string of at most 500 characters and that filters is a record of unknown values, then builds %query% LIKE conditions over the title, case number, summary, headnote and full text without escaping the percent and underscore wildcards, and casts the filter values to the tribunal and precedent value enums without validating them, so an invalid enum value reaches the database as a 500 and a broad pattern scans the whole text column.

POST /api/precedents inserts the typed decision into the library that every organization reads, with the full text, grievor and parties as typed, is_public defaulting to true, no source or import provenance and no organization on the row (the organization appears only in the audit row), after a single role-title check (content_manager) and with no review, redaction or consent step.

PUT /api/precedents/jurisdiction-preferences selects the caller row and then updates or inserts it, but member_jurisdiction_preferences declares no unique index on user_id and organization_id, so two concurrent first saves insert two rows and GET returns an arbitrary one of them; includeNational and autoApply are written as typed with no boolean check, and no precedent route reads the preferences (only the console components apply them in the browser), so the saved preference filters nothing on the server.

GET /api/profile/roles is the generic CRUD list over the profiles table (readRole member, orgScoped true) although profiles has no organization column, so the tenant predicate is not added, and the low-role guard restricts only callers below steward to their own row: a steward or higher of any organization receives every profile of the platform with email, membership tier, payment provider, Stripe customer and subscription ids, Whop ids, plan dates and credit counters.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A steward or any higher role of any organization calls GET /api/profile/roles and receives every row of the profiles table: each user email, membership tier, payment provider, Stripe customer and subscription ids, Whop ids, plan dates and credit counters; orgScoped true is a no-op because profiles has no organization column and the low-role guard releases a caller at steward and above from the own-row restriction.

potentialImpact.description: Contact addresses and payment-provider identifiers of every user of the platform, across all organizations, are listed to the stewards of any one organization, in pages of up to 100 rows, which exposes customer billing identity and supports phishing and account-linking attacks.

releaseDisposition.justification: A steward is a routine office of every local, the role floor restricts the reader to staff of some organization and not to the owner of the profile, the table has no organization column to scope by, and the profiles row-level-security policy depends on a runtime role the source does not establish for this read; a reachable cross-tenant list of personal and billing identifiers is not contained by a staff role, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The route named profile/roles lists billing profiles (membership tier, payment provider and credits) and holds no role, role assignment or permission data, so a client that expects a role list receives subscription records; its POST is configured at the steward floor but profiles is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance table, so every POST is refused with 403 after the role check, and no route assigns a role.

GET /api/profile/me returns isSuccess true with the message Profile retrieved successfully and data null when the profile query fails or times out: getProfileByUserId catches the lookup error and returns null, so a database failure and a user who has no profile are indistinguishable from each other, and the caller is told the profile was retrieved.

GET /api/reconciliation/process?runId= checks the caller finance:view mandate in the caller own organization and then returns getReconciliationRun(runId), whose query is .where(eq(reconciliationRuns.id, runId)) with no organization condition and which is read through the shared db handle, so an officer of any organization with the commercial_reporting entitlement reads any other organization reconciliation run (totals, variance, counts, run-by user, billing period) by id.
